standard.title: General Requirements for Rotary Hose for Water-Well Drilling Equipment (जल-कूप वेधन उपस्कर के लिए घूर्णी होज़ की सामान्य अपेक्षाएँ)
standard.sector: Mechanical Engineering / Diamond Core and Water Well Drilling

sectional_committee.name: Diamond Core and Water Well Drilling Sectional Committee

standard.description: This Indian Standard prescribes the material specifications, multi-layer construction designs, standard inside diameters (bore sizes), working pressure ratings, safety factors, testing protocols, and coupling requirements for high-pressure flexible rotary drilling hoses (Kelly hoses) used to circulate water-based or oil-based drilling mud between the standpipe and vertically moving swivel on water-well drilling rigs.
standard.scope: This Indian Standard prescribes the material specifications, multi-layer construction designs, standard inside diameters (bore sizes), working pressure ratings, safety factors, testing protocols, and coupling requirements for high-pressure flexible rotary drilling hoses (Kelly hoses) used to circulate water-based or oil-based drilling mud between the standpipe and vertically moving swivel on water-well drilling rigs.

certification.description: Voluntary Product Specification. Manufacturers are highly encouraged to obtain a valid BIS license to print or stamp the prestigious physical ISI 'Standard Mark' directly on the vulcanized rubber outer cover of rotary hoses to certify material grades and pressure testing compliance in the competitive drilling rig market.
requirements: Any numerical value representing the result of a physical dimension, test pressure, or diameter must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.

The inner lining must be fabricated from premium oil-resistant and abrasion-resistant synthetic rubber (such as Nitrile/NBR or HNBR) capable of handling water-based or oil-based muds with a minimum aniline point of 66°C without showing structural softening or swelling.

The hose reinforcement must consist of multiple plies (typically 2 to 6 layers) of high-strength spiral steel wire or steel wire braids, interspersed with heavy-duty synthetic textile fabric plies to ensure maximum burst resistance.
The outer cover must be formed of wrapped weather, ozone, and abrasion-resistant synthetic rubber to protect the steel wire core from UV rays, derrick friction, and structural impacts on-site.
The hose nominal inside diameter (bore size) must strictly match standard metric categories to align with rig manifolds: 50 mm (2 in), 63 mm (2.5 in), 75 mm (3 in), 90 mm (3.5 in), or 100 mm (4 in).

Every finished hose assembly must undergo a factory hydrostatic proof test at 1.5 to 2.0 times the rated working pressure (WP) for a minimum of 10 minutes, demonstrating zero leaks, seepage, or permanent swelling.

To prevent catastrophic on-site failures, the minimum burst pressure (destructive test) of any representative prototype hose assembly must be at least 2.5 times its rated working pressure (e.g., minimum burst of 12,500 psi for a 5,000 psi working hose).
To prevent structural kinking and line constriction, hoses must satisfy minimum bending curves without buckling (e.g., a 100 mm / 4-in hose typically requires a minimum bend radius of 1600 mm).

Hoses must be equipped with factory swaged or built-in end connections containing API line pipe threads, forged hammer unions (e.g., Fig 1002/1502), or flanges, tested simultaneously to ensure zero joint slip.
